subject: Recap & next steps: AveryTech pilot acceptance criteria and observation cadence
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Yang <claire.yang@averytech.com>; Samir Rao <samir@averytech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: AveryTech pilot acceptance criteria and observation cadence

Hi Claire / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clean kickoff for the 4-week pilot: 

1) Pilot scope (what we agreed)
- Inference surface: document summarization API + conversational retrieval assistant on a 250k-doc subset.
- Traffic shape: simulated 500 rps burst tests, steady-state 60 rps.

2) Proposed acceptance KPIs (need your sign-off)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 450 ms for summarization (input tokens up to 1k).
- Throughput: handle sustained 60 rps with <5% throttling/errors.
- Cost guardrail: average inference cost <= $0.0009 per token for the deployed quantized model.
- Quality: ROUGE-L for summaries >= 0.48 vs. your labeled test set; manual QA score >= 4/5 on 30 sampled sessions.

3) Observability & evidence we will deliver
- Streaming traces and token-level latency histograms (dashboard + raw traces).
- Representative inference logs (we'll provide a sample trace file).
- Weekly digest with failure modes + suggested config adjustments.

4) Ownership & roles
- Redwood technical lead: Ben Carter (benchmarks, traces, infra tuning).
- Redwood PM (pilot ops): Lauren Bishop (milestones, acceptance sign-off).
- Avery product lead: Claire Yang (test set, quality sign-off).
- Avery infra contact: Samir Rao (network/ingress tests).

5) Timeline (tentative)
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange test-set & access, finalize KPIs and SLOs.
- Week 1: Baseline runs + low-latency tuning.
- Week 2: Load/throughput tests + cost profiling.
- Week 3: Quality evaluation + final configuration.
- Week 4: Acceptance window and retrospective.

Attachments: RDWD_POC_SLA.xlsx (proposed timing and responsibilities), sample_trace_log.txt (example).

Next actions: Claire to confirm KPIs (especially the ROUGE threshold and cost target) and share the labeled test subset by EOD Tuesday. We’ll schedule a 30m technical kickoff once we have the test set.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Attachment: RDWD_POC_SLA.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Claire Yang <claire.yang@averytech.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: AveryTech pilot acceptance criteria and observation cadence

Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. High level sign-off from our side with two adjustments: 

- Quality: bump ROUGE-L target to 0.50 if the test subset includes the latest product docs (we can provide a filtered set that leans harder on concise summaries). If we see consistent 0.48 we can accept but would flag as "needs improvement".
- Cost: can we include a toggle in the runbook for a higher-cost/high-quality tier (e.g., dequantized model) so we can compare quality delta vs cost? Not a blocking item, but useful for prioritization.

We will share the labeled 300-sample test set (CSV + reference summaries) by Tue 2026-09-01 17:00 PDT. Samir will handle network whitelisting for the pilot IP ranges — Samir, please confirm.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Yang
Senior Product Manager | AveryTech
claire.yang@averytech.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: AveryTech pilot acceptance criteria and observation cadence

Claire — Samir —

Confirming Samir's network notes (Samir: thanks for the quick follow). A couple operational clarifications before we start:

- Load profile: please confirm if the 500 rps burst is 60s or 300s (we assumed 60s in the plan). That affects queueing/backpressure config.
- Test data: please redact any PII before sending the labeled set; if redaction is not possible we can run the tests inside a private VPC option (requires an NDA amendment).

Proposed acceptance matrix (short):
- Latency: p95 <= 450 ms (pass) / 450-600 ms (conditional pass, requires follow-up tuning) / >600 ms (fail).
- Throughput: sustained 60 rps with <5% error (pass) / 5-10% (conditional) / >10% (fail).
- Cost/token: <= $0.0009 (pass) / $0.0009-$0.0012 (conditional) / >$0.0012 (fail).
- Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.50 (pass) / 0.46-0.50 (conditional) / <0.46 (fail).

I will prepare the initial dashboard and raw trace export (JSON) so you can validate the metrics.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks —

Samir confirms 60s burst. We will sanitize the test-set; sending the CSV + references now (shared via Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRdwdPilotPlan). If anything in the set looks off, we’ll rework it quickly.

Agree with Ben’s acceptance matrix. We also like the idea of a runbook toggle for a higher-quality tier — please include a brief section in the Week 1 deliverable that outlines when to flip that and the expected cost bump.

Call to schedule: propose Tue 2026-09-07 10:00am PT for the technical kickoff. If that works we’ll send a calendar invite.

Claire
